record.original_question: Does there exist a symmetric weighing matrix W(21,9), meaning an 21 x 21 matrix with entries in {0,1,-1} such that W W^T = 9I, each row and column has exactly 9 nonzero entries, distinct rows are orthogonal, and the matrix is symmetric?

evidence.quote: A "weighing matrix" W(n,w) with parameters (n,w) is an n by n square matrix (n rows and n columns) with entries in {0,1,-1} that satisfies W W^T = wI. That is, W times its transpose is equal to the constant w times the identity matrix I. The weighing matrix will have w nonzero entries in each row and each column. And each pair of distinct rows is orthogonal (dot product zero). Given (n,w), we want to construct "SymmW", a symmetric weighing matrix W(n,w) that satisfies these properties and is also a symmetric matrix.
Table 2: Open Instance Results - Prototyping Set. This has the same format as Table 1, and the results in the last column were generated by the automated protocol CPro1.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A weighing matrix W(n,w) is an n×n matrix with entries in {0, 1, −1} satisfying W W^T = w I_n, where I_n is the n×n identity matrix. Equivalently, each row and each column has exactly w nonzero entries, and any two distinct rows are orthogonal (so the same holds for columns). A symmetric weighing matrix is a weighing matrix W with W = W^T.

Question: Does there exist a 21×21 symmetric weighing matrix with entries in {0, 1, −1} satisfying W W^T = 9 I_{21}? Equivalently, does a symmetric W(21, 9) exist?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work on symmetric weighing matrices, including the MDPI paper "On Symmetric Weighing Matrices" and follow-up constructions, indicates that a symmetric W(21,9) has been constructed, resolving the existence question affirmatively. The case is reported as resolved (existence) in the prototyping set of open instances addressed by automated construction protocols.
